records.name: Dautartas
records.facts_used: Pakerys includes Dautartas among Lithuanian two-stem names with Dau-. He reports the view that Dau- developed from Daug-, connected with daug, “much, many”. Salys connects the name element Tar(t)- with tarti, “to say”, but this does not supply a fixed literal sentence for the whole name. The Senn–Salys dictionary of 1968 lists Dautartas as both a personal name and a surname; the entry was reprinted in 1983. Pakerys discusses its accentuation in 2010. These dated linguistic records establish the exact form, not its first birth registration or a particular medieval bearer.
records.reason: Exact-form evidence supports a two-paragraph history in all five languages.
records.uncertainties: Checked location: Pakerys PDF 4 / printed 91; Salys PDF 295 / printed 280; dictionary PDF 224 / printed 209. Catalogue material is an attributed online transcription; dictionary PDF spellings were visually inspected where used.

records.name: Sulvi
records.facts_used: Rajandi regards Sulvi as more likely a variant of Silvi than a feminine counterpart of Sulev. His wording is comparative, so it does not establish a unique origin for every bearer or justify assigning Sulev’s proposed meaning to Sulvi. His 1966 lexicon also records Sulvi with the locator Trt 22, a Tartu record of 1922. This gives a dated example of the exact spelling. It is a record cited by a later dictionary, rather than an independently inspected birth register or a date when the name was invented.

records.name: Sula
records.facts_used: Rajandi’s lexicon directs the feminine name Sula to Sulev. In the Sulev article he describes an old personal name preserved in folklore and brought into given-name use through literature. He does not establish a single certain lexical origin for that older name. Sula is explicitly listed in the 1966 book, with an older name-list reference in its index. This documents the feminine form itself. Sulev’s nineteenth-century calendar dates belong to Sulev; they cannot be presented as the first calendar appearance of Sula.
